Earnings Review: Above expectations; very positive, including mention of further expediting production capacity increase; maintain Neutral but raise TP, expect share price rebound
12m Price Target: ¥40,000
Upside: 60.5%

1Q results, full-year guidance stronger than expected 1Q operating profits of ¥190 bn, reported after the July 29 close, beat our estimate of ¥152 bn and the Bloomberg consensus of a little under ¥160 bn. Advantest revised up FY3/27 operating profit guidance to ¥846 bn from initial guidance of ¥627.5 bn, well above our prior estimate of ¥751.4 bn and the Bloomberg consensus of a little under ¥710 bn. While trade statistics from various countries likely made the stock market aware of the possibility that 1Q progress could be slightly better than management's assumptions, expectations for a large beat were unlikely to have been high, as recent GPU test times have not changed substantially. As such, we believe this came as an overall positive surprise.
Key points from the results briefing

(1) TAM outlook: Advantest raised its CY26 TAM outlook versus its April forecast for SoC testers by US$1.9 bn, and for memory testers by US$0.3 bn (both based on the midpoint of the range). The primary driver of the revision is chip volumes mainly for inference AI-oriented ASICs, CPUs, and DRAM tracking above expectations. The company noted that while CPU test times are on par with or slightly longer than for GPUs/ASICs in wafer testing, they are somewhat shorter in package testing.
(2) Market share: In SoC testers, Advantest's share is on an uptrend from
in CY25. The gap versus other companies is widening, especially in the AI/HPC space where Advantest has a high share, and the company is looking to capture a market share of at least
in SoC testers overall in the medium term. In memory testers, market share could decline slightly in CY26 (from
in CY25) because of recovery in the NAND segment, where the company's presence is relatively weak, but management plans to leverage new product launches to expand its share going forward.
NEUTRAL

(3) Production capacity: With strong demand likely to continue (demand visibility from customers is around 18 months), Advantest expects to reach its SoC tester production capacity target of 5,000 units by end-FY3/27 sooner rather than later, and is proceeding with capacity expansion ahead of its April plan to expand to 10,000 units by end-2028 or early 2029. The company is also working to expand memory tester production capacity along similar lines to its SoC tester plans.

(4) Profit margins: 1Q gross margin reached a record high of 69.5%, partly from the product mix and inventory valuation gains/losses. While tailwinds for the product mix are likely to persist as strong demand for SoC testers is expected to continue going forward, management expects margins to decline into 2H, partly from the impact of higher procurement costs for items such as DRAM (the company said that it expects memory prices to continue to rise into FY3/28).

Investment Thesis - Advantest

We are Neutral rated on Advantest as we believe the market has now fully recognized the story of expanding semiconductor tester demand, primarily for AI/HPC applications. While we expect volume-based demand growth for AI semiconductors (mainly GPUs and ASICs) and the uptrend in test content to continue, we believe it is unlikely that expectations for GPU/ASIC test times will rise further. Given that the company's earnings growth rate from FY3/28 onward is unlikely to stand out as exceptionally high within our coverage, and in view of the potential for further expansion in SG&A expenses (primarily R&D) to maintain and strengthen competitiveness going forward, we maintain our view that scope for further valuation expansion is limited.
Price Target Risks and Methodology - Advantest

Valuation methodology: Our 12-month target price of ¥40,000 is based on the global SPE sector average EV/EBITDA of 18X (to which we add a 40% sector-relative premium) and our FY3/28E EBITDA estimates (implies FY3/28E P/E of 36X and P/B of 18X).
Key risks: Market share fluctuations, fluctuations in customer capex appetite, trends in tester demand for China, USD/JPY fluctuations.

GS Factor Profile

The GS Factor Profile provides investment context for a stock by comparing key attributes to the market (i.e. our universe of rated stocks) and its sector peers. The four key attributes depicted are: Growth, Financial Returns, Multiple (e.g. valuation) and Integrated (a composite of Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple). Growth, Financial Returns and Multiple are calculated by using normalized ranks for specific metrics for each stock. The normalized ranks for the metrics are then averaged and converted into percentiles for the relevant attribute. The precise calculation of each metric may vary depending on the fiscal year, industry and region, but the standard approach is as follows:

Growth is based on a stock's forward-looking sales growth, EBITDA growth and EPS growth (for financial stocks, only EPS and sales growth), with a higher percentile indicating a higher growth company. Financial Returns is based on a stock's forward-looking ROE, ROCE and CROCI (for financial stocks, only ROE), with a higher percentile indicating a company with higher financial returns. Multiple is based on a stock's forward-looking P/E, P/B, price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

Financial Returns and Multiple use the GS analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics).
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative.
M&A Rank

Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2 representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.

Multiple is based on a stock's forward-looking P/E, P/B, price/dividend (P/D), EV/EBITDA, EV/FCF and EV/Debt Adjusted Cash Flow (DACF) (for financial stocks, only P/E, P/B and P/D), with a higher percentile indicating a stock trading at a higher multiple. The Integrated percentile is calculated as the average of the Growth percentile, Financial Returns percentile and (100% - Multiple percentile).

Financial Returns and Multiple use the GS analyst forecasts at the fiscal year-end at least three quarters in the future. Growth uses inputs for the fiscal year at least seven quarters in the future compared with the year at least three quarters in the future (on a per-share basis for all metrics).
For a more detailed description of how we calculate the GS Factor Profile, please contact your GS representative.
M&A Rank

Across our global coverage, we examine stocks using an M&A framework, considering both qualitative factors and quantitative factors (which may vary across sectors and regions) to incorporate the potential that certain companies could be acquired. We then assign a M&A rank as a means of scoring companies under our rated coverage from 1 to 3, with 1 representing high (30%-50%) probability of the company becoming an acquisition target, 2 representing medium (15%-30%) probability and 3 representing low (0%-15%) probability. For companies ranked 1 or 2, in line with our standard departmental guidelines we incorporate an M&A component into our target price. M&A rank of 3 is considered immaterial and therefore does not factor into our price target, and may or may not be discussed in research.

Quantum is GS' proprietary database providing access to detailed financial statement histories, forecasts and ratios. It can be used for in-depth analysis of a single company, or to make comparisons between companies in different sectors and markets.
